summary_html: Child safely **reunified with parent or guardian**, case closed. Federal policy treats reunification as the preferred outcome once risk factors are mitigated.
authority_html:
- **Adoption and Safe Families Act (ASFA)** — establishes reunification timelines and permanency goals  
- **SSA Title IV-E (42 U.S.C. §§ 670–679c)** — funds reunification services and tracks permanency outcomes

primary_citations.citation_text: Oklahoma - Title 10A (Children and Juvenile Code), § 1-2-101 (Duty to report) and Article 1, Part 4 (deprived child proceedings)
Title 10a: Children and Juvenile Code - CHILD WELFARE PRIMARY

regulations_applicable.title: Title 135 - Commission on Children and Youth

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed orders continuing visitation with a reunification goal and directing a change of foster placement, finding no abuse of discretion in the trial court's weighing of conflicting evidence about the child's best interests.
key_cases.relevance: It is the Oklahoma Supreme Court's statement of how a reunification-directed visitation plan is reviewed when foster caregivers resist it.
key_cases.quote: In making such decisions, the paramount consideration remains the best interests of the child.

key_cases.case_name: State ex rel. Department of Human Services v. Jones (In re T.T.S.)
key_cases.holding: Resolving a split among Court of Civil Appeals panels, the court reversed a termination judgment and held that due process requires the particular conditions a parent failed to correct be specified in the State's application, the jury instructions, the verdict forms and the final order.
key_cases.relevance: Because reunification turns on which conditions must be corrected, the specificity rule here defines what the parent must actually accomplish.
key_cases.quote: Given the gravity of the rights implicated, vigilant enforcement of the full panoply of procedural safeguards must be carried out in child deprivation cases.

key_cases.holding: The court affirmed termination, holding DHS made reasonable reunification efforts despite the absence of visitation the children refused, that clear and convincing evidence supported the jury's verdict, and that trial counsel was effective.
key_cases.relevance: This is the leading recent Oklahoma reasonable-efforts decision and the benchmark for when a reunification plan may be abandoned.
key_cases.quote: We find the district court did not abuse its discretion when it found that DHS made reasonable efforts toward reunification.

key_cases.court: Court of Civil Appeals of Oklahoma
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed a jury verdict terminating a mother's rights to six children, holding DHS's services were adequate despite her claim that trauma-informed care was withheld, and that the heightened ICWA proof requirements were met as to the Indian children.
key_cases.relevance: It sets the Oklahoma benchmark for when a parent's complaint that services were not individualized enough will fail to defeat termination.
key_cases.quote: we find DHS' attempts to help Mother in her efforts to reunite with the children were more than adequate

key_cases.holding: In the second B.T.W. appeal the court affirmed a post-appeal permanency order that kept the child with her foster mother, limited the mother to supervised visitation and changed the permanency plan to long-term out-of-home placement, finding reasonable efforts had been made and no abuse of discretion or due process violation.
key_cases.relevance: This is the later B.T.W. decision that supplies the abuse-of-discretion standard for reviewing a reasonable-efforts finding, the standard In re C.M. applies.
key_cases.quote: A trial court's findings concerning visitation and placement of a child previously adjudicated as deprived are matters of equitable cognizance.

extended_foster_care_age: Up to age 21 (voluntary; conditions apply; began 1 July 2026; 10A O.S. § 1-7-112a)

common_failures: Failure to prove unfitness by clear and convincing evidence
Santosky v. Kramer standard not met

timeline_requirements.deadline: 6 months, then every 6 months thereafter; 30 days after a court determination that reasonable efforts to return the child are not required
timeline_requirements.starts_from: Child enters out-of-home placement — the earlier of the adjudication date or 60 days after the child is removed from the home

timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Must file TPR or document compelling reason
